abbreviations.definition: A double-blind study is one in which neither the participant nor any of the investigator or sponsor staff who are involved in the treatment or clinical evaluation of the subjects are aware of the treatment received.

A complaint is any written, electronic, or oral communication that alleges deficiencies related to the identity, quality, purity, durability, reliability, safety or effectiveness, or performance of a drug or drug delivery system.
Adherence to all study-related, good clinical practice, and applicable regulatory requirements.

A data monitoring committee is a group of independent scientists who are appointed to monitor the safety and scientific integrity of a human research intervention, and to make recommendations to the sponsor regarding the stopping of a study for efficacy, or for harms, or for futility. The composition of the committee is dependent upon the scientific skills and knowledge required for monitoring the particular study.
The act of assigning a participant to a treatment. Participants who are enrolled in the study are those who have been assigned to a treatment.

A process by which a participant voluntarily confirms his or her willingness to participate in a particular study, after having been informed of all aspects of the study that are relevant to the participant’s decision to participate. Informed consent is documented by means of a written, signed, and dated informed consent form.
An interim analysis is an analysis of clinical study data, separated into treatment groups, that is conducted before the final reporting database is created/locked.

A pharmaceutical form of an active ingredient or placebo being tested or used as a reference in a clinical trial, including products already on the market when used or assembled (formulated or packaged) in a way different from the authorized form, or marketed products used for an unauthorized indication, or marketed products used to gain further information about the authorized form.
Equivalent to CDISC term “subject”: an individual who participates in a clinical trial, either as recipient of an investigational medicinal product or as a control
The act of determining if an individual meets minimum requirements to become part of a pool of potential candidates for participation in a clinical study.

Treatment-emergent adverse event: An untoward medical occurrence that emerges during a defined treatment period, having been absent pretreatment, or worsens relative to the pretreatment state, and does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment.

notes: Sub-study: page 1 reads verbatim "This study H0P-MC-OA02 (NCT05080660) is a sub-study of Master Protocol H0P-MC-CPMP (NCT05986292)". The document is the intervention-specific appendix (ISA) H0P-MC-OA02 to Master Protocol H0P-MC-CPMP and the OA disease-state addendum (DSA) H0P-MC-CPMP(1); nothing was filled from the master. Deferrals to the master protocol / DSA: the SoA itself (p11: 'This SoA shows visits and procedures unique to the intervention-specific appendix (ISA) H0P-MC-OA02 for LY3526318. Please refer to the CPMP Master Protocol and the OA DSA H0P-MC-CPMP(1) SoAs for additional information.'); clinical laboratory tests (p30, Appendix 1: 'The CPMP Master Protocol describes tests that may be performed at additional times noted in the SoA for this ISA. This table describes tests unique for ISA OA02.' - the table lists only LY3526318 concentration and Urine pregnancy, so the composition of the SoA rows Hematology, Chemistry, Lipid panel, Urinalysis and HbA1c, and the specimen/lab for all lab rows, is not given in this document); objectives and endpoints (p8, p18); overall design (p19); eligibility (p21); preparation/handling (p23); concomitant therapy (p24); discontinuation (p25); study assessments timing, efficacy assessments and AEs (p26: 'See the CPMP Master Protocol for additional details.'); statistics (p28-29). Efficacy instruments are not described in this ISA (p26 says only 'Planned time points for all efficacy assessments are provided in the SoAs'); the NRS diary (p19) and the WOMAC Pain Subscale Score (p28, key secondary endpoint) are named but no ISA SoA row is linked to them, so their soa_activities are empty; p17 mentions 'OA-associated questionnaires' without naming them. SoA rows the text does not describe: Hematology, Chemistry, Lipid panel, Urinalysis, HbA1c (deferred to master); Participant returns device (the device is not named and its SoA Notes cell is redacted 'CCI' on p12); Intervention compliance is described in Section 6.4 (p23: direct questioning, counting returned capsules) - not an instrument or measurement, so not recorded. Conflict recorded (rule 5): Urine pregnancy - SoA/Appendix 1 give urine (p11, p30), while Appendix 2 contraception guidance (p32) states 'Negative urine result at screening followed by a negative serum result within 24 hours prior to treatment exposure. Note: Subsequent pregnancy testing is compound specific.' Both entries recorded. Inconsistency in Appendix 4 (p40): 'Schedule of Activities as described in the CPMP Master Protocol, CPMP(3) DSA, and NP02 ISA' names a different DSA/ISA than this document (OA DSA CPMP(1), ISA OA02). Abbreviations: Appendix 5 list (p41-43) recorded one entry per line, including the definitional terms; OA is printed twice on p42 and recorded twice. The SoA footnote (p12) defines ED, HbA1c, V and PK = 'pharmacokinetic' (the list has PK = 'pharmacokinetics'); these four are recorded from p12 in the letter-spaced spelling of that page's text layer (the checker needs the text-layer string); the first entry of the p12 footnote is redacted (CCI). Other abbreviations defined under tables (PO, QD on p9/p23; IMP, NA, NIMP on p23; PDEP, V on p10; OA, PK on p18) are not SoA/lab-table abbreviations and are not recorded separately, except where already in the list. All tokens in SoA activity names (ECG, HbA1c, PK) are defined (ECG and PK in the list, HbA1c only in the SoA footnote). Text layer: many pages (e.g. 2, 7-9, 12-16, 19-24, 27-30, 35-39) have a letter-spaced text layer; quotes from these pages are copied as the text layer has them. No page lacks a text layer. Many passages are redacted (CCI/PPD), including dose levels, part of Section 2.3.1, 4.3, 5.2 and Appendix 3. Rule 10: the lab-tests table on p30 was checked against the page image (single column 'Other Tests' with two rows; no column run-together); p12 (SoA continuation) was also viewed to confirm the redacted rows. Protocol version: the PDF holds a single version, ISA H0P-MC-OA02 Amendment (a), approved 10-Aug-2021 (original protocol 04-Jun-2021 per the document history on p4); the SoA comes from this version. Central vs local lab is stated only for exceptional circumstances (p39: local laboratory testing may be conducted in lieu of central laboratory testing), not for any SoA row. Updated 2026-11-07 to schema 1.1 (no re-extraction): instruments carry kind; letter-spaced abbreviation terms and definitions re-spaced (whitespace only, checked from page images).
